name: Rebecca Horn
milestone_by_age_26: Produced her first body sculptures in 1968 at age 24, launching the 'Personal Art' series (1968-72) that established her signature artistic vocabulary of bodily extensions and prosthetics.
early_history_summary: Horn grew up in post-war Germany and was taught to draw by her Romanian governess. She contracted tuberculosis as a teenager and severe lung inflammation from fiberglass at age 20, spending a year in a sanatorium where she began making soft sculptures and body-focused drawings that became the foundation of her art practice.
family_context_summary: Born to industrialist parents in Michelstadt, Germany; grandfather owned a textile factory in Bad König. Parents died when she was 20.
primary_early_advantage_tags: illness, sanatorium, body art, post-war Germany
evidence_summary: Rebecca Horn's artistic direction was profoundly shaped by adversity: tuberculosis as a teenager and severe lung inflammation from fiberglass at age 20 led to a year in a sanatorium, where she began making body-focused sculptures. Her family were industrialists in post-war Germany, and she attended the Hamburg Academy of Fine Arts from 1963. By 1968, at age 24, she produced her first body sculptures, establishing the artistic vocabulary that would define her career.
starting_point: Born to an industrialist family in Michelstadt, Germany; grandfather owned a textile factory in Bad König.
current_position: Died September 6, 2024, at age 80 in Bad König, Hesse, Germany; final role as internationally renowned installation and performance artist.

trajectory.event: Produced her first body sculptures, beginning the 'Personal Art' series that established her artistic direction.
Created Einhorn (Unicorn), one of her most famous performance pieces, a horn worn on the head during a walk through a field.
Youngest participant at documenta 5 in Kassel, presenting Unicorn and other body extension works.
Directed her first film Der Eintänzer, expanding her practice into filmmaking.
Took over a professorship at the Berlin University of the Arts, cementing her institutional standing.
Died in Bad König, Hesse, Germany, leaving a legacy as one of Germany's foremost contemporary artists.

name: Julie Andrews
milestone_by_age_26: Made her Broadway debut starring as Polly in 'The Boy Friend' in September 1954 at age 18, an overnight success that led directly to her casting as Eliza Doolittle in 'My Fair Lady' (1956).
early_history_summary: Andrews began performing professionally at age 12 in the 'Starlight Roof' revue at London's Hippodrome Theatre and became the youngest solo performer at a Royal Command Performance at age 13. Discovered for Broadway by director Vida Hope, she was brought from London to star in 'The Boy Friend,' which became an overnight hit and launched her international career.
family_context_summary: Born to a teacher father and pianist mother who divorced when she was 4; mother married Ted Andrews, a Canadian tenor who gave Julie singing lessons and performed with her in music halls.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a pianist and stepfather Ted Andrews was a tenor who performed in music halls; the family traveled England performing together, and Ted gave Julie professional singing lessons from a young age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: vocal prodigy, music hall family, West End, Broadway, singing lessons
evidence_summary: Julie Andrews was a vocal prodigy whose cords had developed to adult level by age 8, leading to professional singing lessons from Madame Stiles-Allen. She grew up in a performing family — her mother was a pianist and her stepfather a tenor — and began performing professionally at 12 in London's West End. By 18, she was starring on Broadway in 'The Boy Friend,' and at 20 she originated Eliza Doolittle in 'My Fair Lady,' one of the most celebrated Broadway roles ever.
starting_point: Born in Walton-on-Thames, Surrey, to a teacher father and pianist mother; parents divorced when she was 4 and mother married music hall tenor Ted Andrews who trained Julie's voice.
current_position: Dame Julie Andrews, DBE; living at age 90; Academy Award-winning actress and singer; net worth estimated ~$30M; resides in the United States.

trajectory.event: Made professional debut in the 'Starlight Roof' revue at London's Hippodrome Theatre, performing for a full year.
Became the youngest solo performer ever to participate in a Royal Command Performance.
Made Broadway debut starring as Polly in 'The Boy Friend,' an overnight success that launched her international career.
Originated the role of Eliza Doolittle in 'My Fair Lady' on Broadway, becoming a major star.
Starred as Queen Guinevere in 'Camelot' on Broadway, earning another Tony nomination.
Won the Academy Award for Best Actress for 'Mary Poppins,' her film debut.
Starred in 'The Sound of Music,' one of the highest-grossing films of all time.
Made a Dame (DBE) by Queen Elizabeth II in the New Year Honours.

name: Aleksandr Dugin
milestone_by_age_26: Dugin joined the far-right Pamyat organization in 1987 at age 25 and served on its Central Council in 1988-89, but his major intellectual contributions — 'Foundations of Geopolitics' (1997) and co-founding the National Bolshevik Party (1993) — all came after age 26. No material career milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Dugin was born into a military intelligence family in Moscow and joined the occult dissident Iuzhinskii Circle as a teenager. He was expelled from the Moscow Aviation Institute after a KGB arrest in 1983 and worked as a street cleaner before emerging as a leader of Pamyat in 1987.
family_context_summary: Born into a privileged family as the son of a GRU colonel-general; father left the family when Dugin was 3 but ensured a good standard of living.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a colonel-general in Soviet military intelligence (GRU); grandfather and great-grandfather were also military officers.

name: Jean Tabary
milestone_by_age_26: Made his professional comics debut with 'Richard et Charlie' published in the Franco-Belgian comics magazine Vaillant on November 5, 1956, at age 26, launching a career that would span over five decades.
early_history_summary: Tabary was born in Stockholm to a French family, one of nine children. After working various jobs as a young adult including as a plasterer (staffeur), he presented his work to the editorial team at Vaillant magazine, which led to his first published comic strip in 1956.
family_context_summary: Born in Stockholm as one of nine children; father was a professional musician (violinist) and mother was a homemaker. Two of his brothers also became illustrators and draftsmen.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a professional violinist; two brothers became illustrators and draftsmen, suggesting an artistic family environment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Franco-Belgian comics, artistic family, Vaillant magazine
evidence_summary: Jean Tabary was born in Stockholm to a large artistic family — his father was a professional violinist and two brothers became illustrators. After working as a plasterer, he taught himself comics art and pitched to Vaillant magazine, debuting professionally at age 26 in 1956. His major success came later with Totoche (1959) and especially Iznogoud (1962), created with writer René Goscinny.
starting_point: Born in Stockholm as one of nine children to a professional violinist father and homemaker mother; family was French.
current_position: Died August 18, 2011, at age 81 in Saint-Jean-d'Angle, France; final role as celebrated Franco-Belgian comics artist, best known for Iznogoud.

trajectory.event: Made professional comics debut with 'Richard et Charlie' in Vaillant magazine, launching his career.
Created the hit series 'Totoche' in Vaillant, which ran for decades and spawned a spin-off.
Began collaboration with René Goscinny creating Iznogoud, which became his most famous series.
Moved Iznogoud to Pilote magazine, expanding its readership significantly.
Took over Iznogoud solo after Goscinny's death, continuing the series for decades.
Suffered a stroke and stopped drawing; passed Iznogoud to his children.
Died in Saint-Jean-d'Angle, Charente-Maritime, France.

name: Bjørn Wirkola
milestone_by_age_26: Became World Champion at the 1966 FIS Nordic World Ski Championships in Oslo, winning gold in both the large hill and normal hill competitions at age 22, and set his first world record at 146 meters the same year.
early_history_summary: Wirkola grew up in Alta, Norway, where his father was an active sportsman in Nordic combined and football. He began as a Nordic combined skier, winning junior championships in 1962-63, before switching exclusively to ski jumping in 1965. In his first season as a pure ski jumper he won the Norwegian championship and his first Four Hills event.
family_context_summary: Born in Alta, Finnmark, Norway; father was an active sportsman who competed in Nordic combined skiing and played football as a goalkeeper. The community had a strong sports culture.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an active Nordic combined skier and football goalkeeper, providing early exposure to competitive winter sports in a community where skiing was ubiquitous.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norwegian ski jumping, Alta, Nordic combined background, Holmenkollen
evidence_summary: Bjørn Wirkola grew up in Alta, Norway, immersed in the country's ski jumping culture, with a father who competed in Nordic combined. He began as a Nordic combined skier, winning junior titles in 1962-63, then switched to pure ski jumping in 1965. By 1966, at age 22, he was World Champion in both hills and set his first world record, becoming the dominant ski jumper of his era with three consecutive Four Hills Tournament wins (1967-69).
starting_point: Born in Alta, Finnmark, Norway; father was an active Nordic combined skier and football goalkeeper in a community with a strong winter sports culture.
current_position: Living at age 82; retired Norwegian ski jumper and footballer; awarded the Holmenkollen medal (1968) and Egebergs Ærespris (1971); resides in Norway.

trajectory.event: Won junior championships in both Nordic combined and ski jumping, marking his emergence as a top prospect.
Switched exclusively to ski jumping and won the Norwegian championship and his first Four Hills event in Bischofshofen.
Became World Champion in Oslo, winning gold in both large and normal hills, and set his first world record at 146 meters.
Won his first Four Hills Tournament overall title, the first of three consecutive wins.
Awarded the Holmenkollen medal and carried the Norwegian flag at the Grenoble Olympics, finishing fourth.
Set two more world records (156m and 160m) in Planica and won his third consecutive Four Hills Tournament.
Awarded the Egebergs Ærespris, Norway's highest multi-sport honor, for achievements in ski jumping and football.

name: Gabor Maté
milestone_by_age_26: Maté graduated with a B.A. from UBC and worked as a high school English teacher in his twenties, but did not obtain his M.D. until 1977 (age 33) and published his first book after age 50. No material career milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Maté was born in Budapest to a Jewish family in 1944; his maternal grandparents were killed in Auschwitz. The family immigrated to Canada in 1956-57. He studied English and history at UBC, wrote for the student newspaper, and worked as a high school teacher before entering medical school at age 28.
family_context_summary: Born to a Jewish family in Budapest, Hungary; maternal grandparents killed in Auschwitz; family immigrated to Canada in 1956-57 when he was 12-13.
parent_family_domain_summary: Maternal grandfather was a physician, which Maté cited as an influence on his desire to become a doctor, though this connection was severed by the Holocaust.

name: Leila Khaled
milestone_by_age_26: Hijacked TWA Flight 840 on August 29, 1969, at age 25 as part of a PFLP operation, an event that made her internationally known and the subject of a widely reproduced photograph holding an AK-47.
early_history_summary: Khaled was born in Haifa and fled to Lebanon as a refugee at age 4 in 1948. She joined the Arab Nationalist Movement at 15, enrolled at the American University of Beirut at 19, and worked as a teacher in Kuwait before joining the PFLP upon its founding in December 1967. She was selected for the 1969 hijacking operation by PFLP leader Wadi Haddad.
family_context_summary: Born in Haifa, Mandatory Palestine to Arab parents; family fled to Lebanon in 1948 as refugees, leaving her father behind. The family settled in Tyre, Lebanon.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Her brother was also involved in the Arab Nationalist Movement.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Palestinian refugee, PFLP, displacement, activism, hijacking
evidence_summary: Leila Khaled was born in Haifa and became a refugee at age 4 when her family fled to Lebanon in 1948. She joined the Arab Nationalist Movement at 15 and the PFLP at 23. At 25, she participated in the hijacking of TWA Flight 840, which made her internationally known. Her trajectory was entirely shaped by the displacement and dispossession of her family and people.
starting_point: Born in Haifa, Mandatory Palestine to Arab parents; family became refugees in 1948, settling in Tyre, Lebanon, after fleeing the war.
current_position: Living at age 81; member of the PFLP; resides in Amman, Jordan; remains an active Palestinian political figure.

trajectory.event: Joined the Arab Nationalist Movement, following her brother's involvement in Palestinian activism.
Joined the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) upon its founding in December 1967.
Hijacked TWA Flight 840 as part of a PFLP operation, becoming internationally known after a famous photograph circulated worldwide.
Attempted hijacking of an El Al flight; her companion was killed and she was arrested in London, later released in a prisoner exchange.
Published her memoir 'My People Shall Live' with George Hajjar, cementing her public profile.

name: Abu Qatada
milestone_by_age_26: Abu Qatada obtained his Bachelor's in Islamic jurisprudence in Jordan in 1984 (age 23-24) and was preaching to large crowds by age 17, but his major influence as an Islamist ideologue came in the 1990s in London. No material career-defining milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born Omar Mahmoud Othman in Bethlehem, he grew up in Amman, Jordan, and began preaching at Dawa meetings at age 17 to crowds of up to 3,000. He obtained his Bachelor's in Islamic jurisprudence in 1984 and later went to Peshawar, Pakistan, where he earned a Master's and became a lecturer.
family_context_summary: Born in Bethlehem to a family that ran a falafel restaurant; family resettled in Amman, Jordan, as refugees after the 1967 war.

name: Joel Aguilar
milestone_by_age_26: Aguilar became a FIFA listed international referee in 2002 at age 27, just after the age-26 cutoff. His first major tournament assignment was the 2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Aguilar is a Salvadoran football referee who became active in officiating around 2001 and was FIFA listed from 2002 to 2019. His career achievements, including World Cup assignments and CONCACAF Gold Cup finals, all came after age 26.

name: Igor Vori
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2003 World Championship with Croatia at age 22, followed by the Olympic gold medal at the 2004 Athens Olympics at age 24, establishing himself as one of the world's best line players before 26.
early_history_summary: Vori started playing handball relatively late at age 14 in Sesvete, inspired by Croatia's 1996 Olympic gold. He joined RK Zagreb's youth system at 17 and progressed through the ranks to the senior team, winning four league and three cup titles before moving to Italian clubs and returning to Zagreb. He debuted for the Croatian national team in 2001.
family_context_summary: Born in Zagreb, SR Croatia, SFR Yugoslavia; grew up in Sesvete near Zagreb. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: RK Zagreb, Croatian handball, height advantage, late starter, Olympic gold
evidence_summary: Igor Vori started handball late at 14, inspired by Croatia's 1996 Olympic gold, and joined RK Zagreb at 17. Despite initial struggles, coaches Boris Dvoršek and Lino Červar developed him into a top pivot. By 22, he was a World Champion, and at 24 he won Olympic gold, leveraging his 2.03m height and the Croatian handball pipeline that produced multiple generations of champions.
starting_point: Born in Zagreb, SR Croatia, SFR Yugoslavia; grew up in Sesvete near Zagreb; started playing handball at 14 inspired by Croatia's 1996 Olympic gold.
current_position: Living at age 45; current coach of Croatian handball club MRK Sesvete; retired as player in 2019 after career spanning RK Zagreb, Barcelona, HSV Hamburg, and PSG.

trajectory.event: Began senior handball career with RK Zagreb, winning four league and three cup titles over four years.
Made debut for the Croatian national team, beginning an international career spanning 246 caps.
Won the World Championship with Croatia, establishing himself as an elite line player.
Won Olympic gold medal at the Athens Olympics with Croatia.
Joined FC Barcelona, one of Europe's top handball clubs.
Named World Championship MVP and won silver medal; voted best defensive player at the 2008 European Championship.
Won Olympic bronze medal at the London Olympics with Croatia.

name: Nicko McBrain
milestone_by_age_26: McBrain played in pub bands from age 14 and did session work including the UK #14 single 'Nice One Cyril' (1973) and was a member of Streetwalkers (1975), but his career-defining role as Iron Maiden's drummer did not begin until 1982 at age 30. No material career-defining milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: McBrain was born in Hackney, London, and began drumming at age 10. He played in pub bands from 1966, did session work including the 1973 hit 'Nice One Cyril,' and joined Streetwalkers in 1975 before stints with McKitty and Trust. He joined Iron Maiden in 1982, replacing Clive Burr.
family_context_summary: Born in Hackney, London; father bought him his first drum kit at age 11-12. Family background otherwise not documented in reviewed sources.

name: Salvatore Sciarrino
milestone_by_age_26: Held his first public concert in 1962 at age 15, with his composition 'Frammento op. 1' performed in Palermo, and was published by the major music publisher Ricordi from 1969 (age 22), establishing his professional compositional career well before 26.
early_history_summary: Sciarrino was born in Palermo and began composing at age 12 as a self-taught musician, though he had some private lessons with Antonino Titone and Turi Belfiore. He was immersed in Palermo's Settimane Internazionali Nuova Musica festival, which provided a culturally vibrant context for his early development. By 1966, he considered his personal style to have emerged, and he was published by Ricordi from 1969.
family_context_summary: Born in Palermo, Sicily; attracted to visual arts before turning to music. Family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught, Palermo, new music, Ricordi, early composition
evidence_summary: Salvatore Sciarrino began composing at 12 as a self-taught musician in Palermo, benefiting from the city's Settimane Internazionali Nuova Musica festival and some private lessons with Antonino Titone and Turi Belfiore. His first public concert was at 15 in 1962, and by 1966 his personal style had emerged. From 1969, he was published by Ricordi, one of the most prestigious music publishers, establishing his professional career by age 22.
starting_point: Born in Palermo, Sicily; attracted to visual arts before turning to music at age 12; largely self-taught as a composer.
current_position: Living at age 78; described as 'the best-known and most performed Italian composer' of the present day; resides in Città di Castello, Umbria, Italy.

trajectory.event: Held his first public concert in Palermo, with his composition 'Frammento op. 1' performed.
Composed the Sonata for two pianos, which he considers the beginning of his official catalog and personal style.
Published by Ricordi, a major music publisher, and moved to Rome to study electronic music with Franco Evangelisti.
Moved to Milan and began teaching composition at the conservatory.
Composed the opera Lohengrin, expanding his output into major theatrical works.
Composed two major operas, Infinito nero and Luci mie traditrici, cementing his reputation in contemporary opera.
